body.summary: Reverb — halls, rooms, chambers, plates, springs and more, with multi-band decay, EQ, ducking, modulation and pitch.
body.detail: Type recalls a mix-ready space instantly; the Basic/EQ/Advanced pages tailor decay, tone and character.

0.blurb: Selects the space — Hall, Room, Chamber, Cathedral, Plate, Spring and more.

1.blurb: Decay (t60) time — how long the tail takes to fade out.

2.blurb: High-cut on the wet signal only — darkens the reverb without dulling the dry tone.

3.blurb: High-band decay relative to overall time; shorten it to model an absorptive room.

5.blurb: Size of the modeled space. Larger spaces are darker and grainier; very small values turn metallic.

7.blurb: Level of the early reflections (no effect on Spring types).

9.blurb: Gap before the reverb starts; keeps a small space yet pushes the tail back from the dry signal.

10.blurb: Low-cut on the wet signal only — keeps the reverb from muddying the mix.

11.blurb: Modulation depth in the tail — thickens and lushes up the reverb, chorus-like.

12.blurb: Modulation rate of the tail movement.

13.blurb: Wet/dry blend. 0% = dry only, 100% = effect only.

15.blurb: Places the block output in the stereo field.

16.blurb: How the signal is routed when bypassed (e.g. muted, thru, or kept wet for trails).

17.blurb: Adds a global offset to this block’s Mix across all presets.

19.blurb: Echo density of the tail. Higher = smoother; lower lets individual repeats show.

33.blurb: Decay time of the low band — set independently for natural multi-band tails.

34.blurb: Crossover frequency splitting the low/high decay bands.

36.blurb: Ducker depth — how much the reverb dips while you play. 0 disables ducking.

37.blurb: Input level above which the ducker attenuates the reverb.

44.blurb: HOLD sustains the current tail indefinitely; STACK holds it but keeps the input open to layer.

47.blurb: Selects which input(s) feed the block (left, right, sum, or stereo).

51.blurb: When on, this block ignores scene changes.

52.blurb: Removes the dry signal so only the wet effect is heard — useful in parallel/wet-only routings.

REVERB_SIZE.blurb: Size of the modeled space. Larger spaces are darker and grainier; very small values turn metallic.

REVERB_LFXOVER.blurb: Crossover frequency splitting the low/high decay bands.

REVERB_LFTIME.blurb: Decay time of the low band — set independently for natural multi-band tails.

REVERB_HFRATIO.blurb: High-band decay relative to overall time; shorten it to model an absorptive room.

REVERB_EARLYLEVEL.blurb: Level of the early reflections (no effect on Spring types).

REVERB_DENSITY.blurb: Echo density of the tail. Higher = smoother; lower lets individual repeats show.

REVERB_DEPTH.blurb: Modulation depth in the tail — thickens and lushes up the reverb, chorus-like.

REVERB_RATE.blurb: Modulation rate of the tail movement.

REVERB_HOLD.blurb: HOLD sustains the current tail indefinitely; STACK holds it but keeps the input open to layer.

REVERB_ATTEN.blurb: Ducker depth — how much the reverb dips while you play. 0 disables ducking.

REVERB_THRESH.blurb: Input level above which the ducker attenuates the reverb.

REVERB_MIX.blurb: Wet/dry blend. 0% = dry only, 100% = effect only.

REVERB_PAN.blurb: Places the block output in the stereo field.

REVERB_BYPASSMODE.blurb: How the signal is routed when bypassed (e.g. muted, thru, or kept wet for trails).

REVERB_GLOBALMIX.blurb: Adds a global offset to this block’s Mix across all presets.

REVERB_INPUTSELECT.blurb: Selects which input(s) feed the block (left, right, sum, or stereo).

REVERB_SCENEIGNORE.blurb: When on, this block ignores scene changes.

REVERB_KILLDRY.blurb: Removes the dry signal so only the wet effect is heard — useful in parallel/wet-only routings.
